findings.title: Old locally-stored recovery codes stay valid when new codes are accepted by the user storage
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`; if the user storage returns `true`, it logs and returns without touching Keycloak's own store. Before this change recovery codes for federated (non-import) users were always written to Keycloak's federated-storage tables via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which also deletes any previously stored recovery-code credential. After upgrading, a federated user who already has such a local credential and regenerates codes will get the new set stored in the user storage while the old set remains in Keycloak DB. `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls through to the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` when the storage rejects the input, so the old, supposedly replaced codes continue to authenticate the user, while the login page (driven by `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which prefers the federated credential) asks for a number from the new set. The method should remove existing stored credentials of this type (e.g. via the credential provider's delete path) when the user storage accepted the new codes.

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById is applied to a credential that may come from the user storage
findings.body: `optUserCredentialFound` is now obtained from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which returns the user-storage credential first. When that credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. A credential produced by a `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials` implementation is not a stored Keycloak credential: its id is provider-defined or null (e.g. `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` never sets an id, as the test provider in this PR shows). With a null id the JPA federated store's `em.find(..., null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, failing the login after the code was already accepted; with a foreign id the call is a silent no-op and the exhausted credential is never cleared in the storage. For federated credentials the removal should go through `disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` (or be skipped), and the local removal should only run for credentials actually obtained from `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream`.

findings.title: User label and generation timestamp are dropped on the user-storage path
findings.body: The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` passed in carries the user-chosen label (`userLabel` hidden field) and the `generatedAt` timestamp, but the `UserCredentialModel` handed to `updateCredential` only contains the type and the JSON list of raw codes. A user storage provider therefore has no way to persist the label or the real generation time (the test provider ends up with `userLabel == null` and `createdDate = now`). When the storage accepts the credential, the label the user typed is silently lost, which is a behavioral regression versus the local path where both are stored.

findings.title: New user-storage SPI contract for recovery codes is undocumented and unverified
findings.body: This method introduces a new, implicit contract for `CredentialInputUpdater` implementations: for type `recovery-authn-codes` the `CredentialInput.getChallengeResponse()` is a JSON-serialized array of plaintext codes, and `getCredentials(realm, user)` is expected to return a `CredentialModel` whose `credentialData`/`secretData` can be parsed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` (otherwise `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` and the authenticator will throw). None of this is documented on the method, in `CredentialInputUpdater`, or in release notes. Additionally, unlike `createOTPCredential` which returns a boolean and validates the result, this method is `void` and trusts a `true` from `updateCredential` without any check, so a provider that answers `supportsCredentialType` liberally but does not persist the codes leaves the user with no recovery codes while the required action is marked complete.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code test covers only a single login; consumption, exhaustion and removal are untested
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes and performs one login with code #0. The companion test storage never marks a code as used (`isValid` is a plain `anyMatch` over all codes), always rebuilds the credential with all codes remaining, never exposes an id, and does not support `disableCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` for this type. Consequently the new production paths are not exercised for federated storage: that the next requested code number advances after use, the `allCodesUsed()` branch in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (which now operates on a federated credential), re-generation replacing an older set, and removal via admin/account REST. A test that re-logs with a second code and asserts the requested code number, plus one exercising exhaustion, would catch the id/removal problem in the authenticator.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check
findings.body: Every other method in this provider (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser(user)` returning null, but `getCredentials` immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes`. `getCredentials` is reached via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` from the account REST endpoint and from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, so a `UserModel` adapter whose backing entry has been removed from the shared map (e.g. after `removeUser` in test cleanup while a session still holds the adapter) produces a `NullPointerException` instead of an empty stream.

findings.title: Recovery-code credential returned from getCredentials has no id; id generated in updateCredential is discarded
findings.body: `updateCredential` assigns `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` to the stored `recoveryCodesModel`, but `getCredentials` rebuilds the credential with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which never sets an id, so consumers receive a credential with `getId() == null`. This makes the credential unaddressable through the account REST API (`/credentials/{id}`) and feeds a null id into `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`'s `removeStoredCredentialById` branch. The stored id (and label) should be copied onto the rebuilt model so the test provider reflects what a real provider must return.
